packet.prompt:
Read only the supplied manuscript images. Do not search for the text, open a
catalogue or edition, or consult an earlier transcription. Do not identify the
work or author. If prior context has already revealed a proposed identification
or reading, stop and report that exposure instead of calling this a blind reading.

Begin with a brief image-only layout survey. Note orientation, columns, running
titles, rubrics, enlarged initials, underlined text, and interlinear or marginal
glosses when visible. Distinguish observations from tentative interpretations
such as main text with commentary. Do not infer author, work, date, or provenance.
A tight crop may not show the layout; say so rather than guessing.

Use those features to choose a few useful spans: headings or question openings,
then connecting prose, transitions or citation chains. Keep quoted lemmata and
commentary separate. Read enough surrounding prose to make a later source match
checkable; a full transcription is not required. State which areas you selected
and which remain unread. Suggest a wider view or an adjacent crop if needed.

Transcribe those spans, preserving physical lines. Label each line with its
image filename and a line number counted from the top of that image. Keep columns
and marginal additions separate. Note overlapping crops rather than treating
repeated lines as additional text.

Retain abbreviation marks when possible. Put proposed expansions in parentheses,
uncertain readings before a question mark, and unreadable text in [illegible].
Describe visible deletions and additions explicitly. Do not supply missing words
from what would make grammatical or philosophical sense. Leave uncertainty visible.

Return the reading as UTF-8 plain text. Include limitations (cropped lines, damage,
uncertain column order) in that same response. This is an unverified image reading.

text:
PACKET-12 - unverified blind image reading

Exposure: nothing in my context proposed an identification or reading of this text. I did nothing beyond the brief, except that I used `ls` on the packet directory to get the image filenames.

LAYOUT SURVEY (image-only)
- There are four overviews: image-001, image-004, image-007 and image-010. They appear to show two small parchment strips (spine-lining or sewing-support strips), each photographed on both faces. Each strip has a braided thread endband or sewing along one long edge.
  - Strip 1: about 9.5 cm x 2 cm. Face 1a is image-001 (tiles 002, 003). Face 1b is image-004 (tiles 005, 006). In image-004 the braid is at the bottom, which suggests the strip was flipped vertically.
  - Strip 2: about 12.5 cm x 1.8 cm. Face 2a is image-007 (tiles 008, 009). Face 2b is image-010 (tiles 011, 012). Face 2b is mostly blank on the visible surface, with a later ink number "95"? or "25"? and a dark round stain. Only a lower folded-over edge carries text.
- Script: a small gothic textualis in black/brown ink, with red touches (a stroked initial, red rubric words). Two columns are visible on strip 1 (a left fragment and a right fragment, separated by an intercolumnium). Strip 2 face 2a shows a column with a large red initial at the left ("D"? or "B"?), a red rubric phrase "?et paulo?" / "?Item pauli?", and a second column to the right.
- The text is too short to establish the genre. Only 2 to 4 partial lines per column survive.
- Selected: every visible line on every face. Unread: lines hidden under the braided sewing, and the cut top/bottom lines.

TRANSCRIPTION
Line numbers count from the top of each tile. Overviews duplicate the tiles.

== Strip 1, face 1a (image-002, image-003) ==
Left column (image-002):
l.1  [under sewing] ?mo? ?uacat? / ?ruinatur? [illegible]
l.2  ?re?gnabit? / ?sigillabit? . ?uos? ?p(er)? ?di-
l.3  ?r?g(u)? lig(?)? . ?d(i)c(itu)r? / ?eius? ?pl(ur)?
l.4  [bottom, cut] [illegible tops]
Right column (image-002 right and image-003):
l.1  [under sewing] ?q(ui)? ?d(?)? ?tenerent? [illegible]
l.2  ?t(un)c? ?tuu(m)? / ?i(n)uice? q(uo)d? ?dar(e)? . [red-touched initial] ?Glau-? / ?Elau-? ?d(?)? ?de? ?si(?)? ?loquitur? / ?expon(itur)?
l.3  ?ueni(?)? ?transitu(m)? / ?caelestia? ?a? ?fra(?)? ?t(e)r(r)a? ?no(n)? ?ad?
l.4  [cut] ?r(?)? ?Sed? ?p(ro)? ?(?)? [illegible]
   Image-003 extends l.2 to the right: "... [red touch] Clau- ... me ?i(n)uocant? / ?sp(iritu)m? [illegible]". After that the strip is blank parchment, folded, with two small holes.

== Strip 1, face 1b (image-005, image-006) ==
Left column (image-005):
l.1  ?p(?)?q(?)? ?q(ui)? ?gener(?)? ?apo? [abraded]
l.2  ?re?cepta? / ?accepta? ?inter? ?o(mn)ia? [illegible]
l.3  ?mul(?)? / ?nulla(m)? ?d(icitu)r? ?& ?p(ro)ca? / ?pra? .
Right column (image-005 right, image-006):
l.1  [red-touched initial] ?Ro? / ?Do? ?u?(?) [abraded] ... ?Diuidunt?/?Dicunt? [illegible] ?neg(?)?
l.2  [red stroke] ?Ista? ?n(on)? ?solu(m)? / ?soluit? ?(?)? [surface flaking] ?enim? ?p(ro)? ?de? ?se? [illegible] ?eum?
l.3  ?Ruo? / ?Suo? ?n(on)? ?(?)? ?enim? ?ex? ?(?)? ?q(ue)?(?) . [red touch] ?Qui? ?neglig(it)? / ?Quod neglig(itur)? ?me?
l.4  [cut] ?d(icitu)r? ?(?)? ?(?)? [illegible]
   On l.3 a superscript "e" is written above, as an interlinear correction or insertion before "Qui neglig(?)". It is uncertain.

== Strip 2, face 2a (image-008, image-009) ==
Left column (image-008):
l.1  ?peccat? ?(?)? ?q(uo)d? ?ac? [under sewing] ?(?)? ?p(ro)dicat? ?et?
l.2  ?clam(?)? / ?clade? ?de? ?eo? [rubric in red, partly under a dark spot:] ?et paulo? / ?Item pauli?
l.3  [large red initial D/B, 2 lines high] ?D?ust? ?(?)? ?uero? / ?n(isi)? ... ?tre? / ?eae? ?d(icitu)r? ?duo?(?) ?z?
l.4  [cut] ?mult(?)? ?(?)? [illegible]
Right column (image-008 right, image-009):
l.1  [under sewing] ?uisitatio? / ?in(?)? ?d(icitu)r? ?(?)? ?de? ?ex? [illegible] ?auxilio?/?annos?
l.2  & ?familie? ?d(?)? ?sciendu(m)? ?q(uo)d? [red touch] ?Ca(usa)? / ?Te(xtus)? ?& ?quia? / ?q(ua)nti?
l.3  ?de? ?ex? ?uoce? / ?d(e)? ?ipsa? ?p(ro)ph(et)ar(um)? / ?pl(ur)?(?) ?& ?relig(?)? ?ad(?)? ?d(icitu)r? / ?ad(?)s(?)?
l.4  [cut] ?Ab? [red dot] ?(?)? ?sunt? [illegible]

== Strip 2, face 2b (image-011, image-012) ==
- Mostly blank parchment (hair side?). It has blue and red pigment specks at the far left, a later ink numeral at the centre ("95"? or "25"?), and a dark round stain or seal mark.
- Along the lower folded edge, one line of text shows upside-down or turned-in (image-011):
  l.1  ?nom(?)? ?B(?)? / ?R(?)? ?(?)? ?q(ue)? ?(?)? ?&? ?luce(m)? / ?lucem? ?(?)?
  Image-012 has only faint ink traces (?"I", "p", "e"?).

LIMITATIONS
- These are extremely small fragments with only 2 to 4 cut lines per column. Most words are partial, and the surface is flaked on strip 1 face 1b.
- The braided sewing covers the top line of strip 1 face 1a and of strip 2 face 2a. Lifting or imaging the area under the thread would recover a line.
- I cannot establish whether strips 1 and 2 come from the same leaf, or which face is recto. Strip 1's orientation on face 1b looks inverted relative to face 1a.
- All readings carry very low confidence. They are given only as possible search strings: "Qui neglig-", "familie", "paulo/pauli" in red.
